newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal's Alardo water returns to market.
newsitem.headline: Portugal's Alardo water returns to market.

text.p: Portuguese authorities lifted a suspension on Thursday in the production and sale of Aguas do Alardo bottled water after tests showed that it was safe for consumption, officials said.
Earlier this month, health authorities ordered a halt to the production and sale of the water produced by the unit of Belgian company Spadel after it was found to contain plankton.

"The company has resumed production after the Directorate-General of Health gave assurances that Aguas do Alardo does not present any risk to health," Pierre de Winter, director-general of Aguas do Alardo, told a news conference.
An official source in the Directorate-General of Health confirmed that the suspension had been lifted.
Tests showed the plankton had presented no risk to public health, the source said. The company has said it was taking steps to eradicate the plankton.

Aguas do Alardo, which bottles water from northern Portugal, accounts for about 13 percent of the local bottled water market and is the second biggest Portuguese producer after Agua do Luso, newspapers said.
